prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1346; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed first notice of loss. Insured reports a collision at an intersection while turning left. Claimant's vehicle was struck on the driver side. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles received from insured.

Entry 2: Contacted the claimant's attorney's office to acknowledge representation. Attorney confirmed the claimant is treating for neck and back strain. All further communication to go through counsel. Requested medical authorization forms and recorded statement scheduling through the attorney.

Entry 3: Received police report. Officer notes the insured was turning left across oncoming traffic and did not yield. Witness statement on file supports the claimant's account of the signal phase. Liability appears probable against the insured, pending review of the scene diagram.

Entry 4: Claimant's counsel sent treatment records and a demand package. Records show initial evaluation at urgent care followed by physical therapy referral for cervical and lumbar strain. No fractures or imaging-confirmed disc injury noted. Referred file to supervisor for evaluation of settlement range and reserve adjustment.

Entry 5: Reserve updated to reflect bodily injury exposure and property damage. Settlement authority requested. Left voicemail with defense counsel on the insured's behalf regarding a possible early resolution. Diary set for follow-up after supervisor review of the treatment file.
